author: reek
body: Compaction must not eat a collection.

author: reek
body: It used to keep ONE FACT PER KIND: it walked the log, dropped any entry whose kind it had already seen, and rewrote what was left. That is right for a kind holding a single current value -- the browser's history blob is rewritten whole, and only the newest matters -- and it destroys any kind holding a collection. Kind 24 is secret ENTRIES. Kind 25 is FileShare manifests. Kind 26 is revocation records. Kind 30 is every source definition in the repository.

author: reek
body: So: write three distinct facts of kind 30, and one exact duplicate of the first. Compaction must keep the three, because nothing on the disk says one supersedes another, and it may collapse the duplicate, because the same kind and the same content hash IS the same fact. Under the old rule this test would report one survivor and two destroyed source files.

author: reek
body: The other half is order. The old walk collected survivors newest-first and rewrote the log in that order, so a compacted log came out REVERSED -- and app-scan-last, which trusts log order to mean recency, would then hand back the OLDEST fact of a kind. Survivors keep their log order here. The copy of alpha that survives is the newest one, so alpha ends up where that copy sat, which is last: beta, gamma, alpha.
